extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and OED/USPTO disciplinary staff
extracted.subtask_short: reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing the USPTO's reciprocal transfer of a registered practitioner to disability inactive status under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29, including notice, opportunity to respond, effects of transfer, and related administrative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for transfer to disability inactive status
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer to disability inactive status is predicated on a state or other tribunal order indefinitely suspending the practitioner from the practice of law due to disability (e.g., "predicated on a May 14, 2015 Order ... which indefinitely suspended Respondent from the practice of law in Texas due to her disability").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.29; the OED Director may file a 'Request for Reciprocal Transfer to Disability Inactive Status' based on such a state order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of Request for Reciprocal Transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director files a 'Request for Reciprocal Transfer to Disability Inactive Status Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29' to initiate transfer proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Request triggers issuance of a Notice and Order to the respondent and begins the procedural steps under § 11.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.29' must be mailed to the respondent (certified mail in this case) and provide the respondent an opportunity to file, within thirty (30) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal transfer to disability inactive status based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery of the Notice is established (e.g., Notice was delivered on May 28, 2016); the respondent's timely response is the mechanism to raise factual or legal issues under § 11.29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond permits finding of no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order, the Office may determine that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.29(d) and proceed to transfer the respondent to disability inactive status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of a response supports resolution of the proceeding without disputed factual issues and justifies issuance of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transfer — prohibition on practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: While on disability inactive status, the practitioner 'shall not be authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters' and is precluded from practice for an indefinite period until further order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer to disability inactive status precludes all practice before the USPTO; effectiveness is from the date of the Final Order until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in Official Gazette and FOIA availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the transfer (including practitioner name and registration number) and stating that the action is predicated on the state order; disciplinary decisions and transfers are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should state the basis for transfer (state order/date) and the practical effect (not authorized to practice before USPTO); provide link/reference to FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and the public under § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the transfer and the reasons for the transfer to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reciprocal and public dissemination of the disciplinary action across jurisdictions and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent duties under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 contains specific duties of practitioners transferred to inactive or suspended status (e.g., notification and handling of client matters); the Final Order expressly imposes compliance with those duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step severs the practitioner's electronic access/association to USPTO systems tied to Customer Numbers and PKI until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on obtaining or being added to Customer Numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall her name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventing acquisition or association with Customer Numbers enforces the practical effect of the disability inactive status on e-filing and electronic representation capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for issuance of Final Order and responsible officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order is issued by the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED Director) and executed by USPTO officials (here signed by Deputy General Counsel on behalf of the Under Secretary/Director), under the authority of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.29.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the statutory and regulatory basis and the USPTO officials responsible for implementing transfers to disability inactive status.
